question.text: The SID of a mutual fund scheme must include a Due Diligence Certificate issued by:

answer.text: SEBI after reviewing the scheme documents
The statutory auditor of the mutual fund

explanation.text: The Logic: The SID is filed with SEBI along with a Due Diligence Certificate from the AMC. SEBI itself has not approved or certified the SID; it only provides observations on the draft. The Trap: SEBI does not issue any certificate. The auditor's role is financial auditing, not document certification. Trustees oversee the AMC but do not issue the Due Diligence Certificate accompanying the SID filing. Note: Remember the pairing: the SID is filed with SEBI, the Due Diligence Certificate accompanying it is issued by the AMC, and SEBI registration does not amount to approval of the scheme.
